title: Excessive log spam when restoring backup that exceeds block storage volume.size
description:
### Please confirm

- [x] I have searched existing issues to check if an issue already exists for the bug I encountered.

### Distribution

Ubuntu

### Distribution version

24.04

### Output of `snap list --all lxd core20 core22 core24 snapd`

```shell
Name    Version         Rev    Tracking       Publisher   Notes
core22  20260225        2412   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
core24  20260317        1588   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
lxd     5.21.4-aee7e08  38779  latest/stable  canonical✓  disabled
lxd     6.7-d814d89     38775  latest/stable  canonical✓  -
snapd   2.74.1          26383  latest/stable  canonical✓  snapd
```

### System info

kernel_version: 6.8.0-106-generic
driver_version: 6.0.6
server_version: "6.7"
Storage backend: lvm

### Instance log

n/a

### Expected behavior

When attempting to restore / import an instance backup that is larger than the storage pool's `volume.size` when using a block-oriented storage, the operation correctly fails. However, the logging is noisy and difficult to read.

As discussed [here](https://discuss.linuxcontainers.org/t/specify-profile-when-restoring-backup/10212/7), block-oriented storage drivers must allocate fixed-size volumes upfront, and the disk fills up completely during unpacking. `tar` then throws a separate error for every subsequent file it attempts to process. LXD captures this entire stderr stream and outputs it as a single massive log entry, which obscures the root cause.

Expected/ideal behaviour is that the daemon should gracefully handle and summarise `tar` errors to maintain readable logs. Ideally, it should detect the `No space left on device` condition and return a single, clean error message to the user, like `Error starting unpack: No space left on device. Storage volume limit exceeded. Consider increasing volume.size on the target pool.`

This both identifies the source of the error, and provides the user with a suggested fix.

### Actual behavior

When importing an instance that will exceed the `volume.size` of the target block-oriented storage, the entire `tar` output is captured and emitted in the logs, producing thousands of individual write failures. The log files produced often reach several megabytes in size for a single failed operation. The failure is expected and correct, however the console spam that the user receives can be difficult to parse and debug.

```
Apr 13 15:25:56 lxd-repro lxd.daemon[5207]: time="2026-04-13T15:25:55+10:00" level=warning msg="Failure for operation" class=task description="Restoring backup" err="Create instance from backup: Error starting unpack: Failed to run: tar -zxf - --xattrs-include=* --restrict --force-local --numeric-owner -C /var/snap/lxd/common/lxd/storage-pools/smallpool/containers/test-import --strip-components=2 backup/container: exit status 2 (tar: rootfs/bigfile: Wrote only 2048 of 10240 bytes
tar: rootfs/bin.usr-is-merged: Cannot mkdir: No space left on device
tar: rootfs/boot: Cannot mkdir: No space left on device
tar: rootfs/dev: Cannot mkdir: No space left on device
tar: rootfs/dev: Cannot mkdir: No space left on device
tar: rootfs/dev/console: Cannot mknod: No such file or directory
tar: rootfs/dev: Cannot mkdir: No space left on device
tar: rootfs/dev/fd: Cannot open: No such file or directory 
[...1000s more omitted...]
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a storage pool using a block-oriented backend (e.g. LVM, Ceph) without setting an explicit `volume.size`, leaving it at the default of 10 GB.
2. Launch an instance against a pool that has sufficient space and write more than 10 GB of data into it.
3. Export the instance as a backup and delete it.
4. Attempt to import the backup into the block-backed pool with the default 10 GB `volume.size`. This import should fail, and the console is spammed with `No such file or directory` for each file that was not able to be created due to limited space.

The minimal Bash script below demonstrates this behaviour using LVM:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# repro.sh:demonstrates log spam on LVM backup restore failure
set -uo pipefail

LOG_FILE="/tmp/lxd-daemon-repro.log"
BIG_IMG="/var/lib/lxd-bigpool.img"
SMALL_IMG="/var/lib/lxd-smallpool.img"

sudo snap install lxd && sudo snap refresh lxd --channel=latest/stable
sudo lxd init --auto

# Craete Big pool (source, 15 GB volumes)
sudo truncate -s 25G "$BIG_IMG"
sudo losetup -f "$BIG_IMG"
BIGLOOP=$(sudo losetup -j "$BIG_IMG" | cut -d: -f1)
sudo lxc storage create bigpool lvm source="$BIGLOOP" lvm.use_thinpool=false volume.size=15GB
sudo lxc profile create bigprofile
sudo lxc profile device add bigprofile root disk path=/ pool=bigpool

# Create original source instance and pack with 11 GB of data
sudo lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 source-instance --profile bigprofile
sleep 10
sudo lxc exec source-instance -- bash -c \
  "dd if=/dev/zero of=/bigfile bs=1M count=11264 status=progress; sync"
sudo lxc export source-instance /tmp/large-backup.tar.gz
sudo lxc delete source-instance --force

# Create target pool (default 10 GB volumes)
sudo truncate -s 20G "$SMALL_IMG"
sudo losetup -f "$SMALL_IMG"
SMALLLOOP=$(sudo losetup -j "$SMALL_IMG" | cut -d: -f1)
sudo lxc storage create smallpool lvm source="$SMALLLOOP" lvm.use_thinpool=false

# Trigger the import (should fail)
BEFORE=$(date --iso-8601=seconds)
sudo lxc import /tmp/large-backup.tar.gz test-import --storage smallpool || true

sleep 2
# Extract logs and check size of log file
sudo journalctl -u snap.lxd.daemon --since "$BEFORE" --no-pager > "$LOG_FILE"
echo "Logs size : $(du -sh "$LOG_FILE")"

```

### Information to attach

- [ ] Any relevant kernel output (`dmesg`)
- [ ] Instance configuration (`lxc config show <instance> --expanded`)
- [ ] Main daemon log (at `/var/log/lxd/lxd.log` or `/var/snap/lxd/common/lxd/logs/lxd.log`)
- [ ] If a lxc command fails, output of the command with `--debug`
- [ ] Output of the daemon with `--debug` (or use `lxc monitor` while reproducing the issue)
